title: [IELTS INSIGHTS JAN 26] - Average commute time & Modes of transport to work in the UK: 2009
prompt: The charts below show UK workers’ average time spent and methods to work in 2009. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie chart compares UK workers’ commute time, while the bar chart shows how they got to work in 2009.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the majority of British workers spent half an hour or less travelling to work, and cars were by far the most commonly used means of transport in both London and across the UK. In addition, nearly twice as many commutes were by car outside London as in London.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding commute times, 42% of UK workers took 1-15 minutes to travel to work on average. Meanwhile, roughly one-third of the country's workforce had 16-30-minute commutes, which was nearly triple the figure for the 31-45-minute range, at 12%. By contrast, longer commutes were relatively uncommon, with 8% of workers or fewer traveling for 45-60 minutes or over an hour.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for travel methods, cars were the primary mode of transport across the UK, being used by 70% of workers outside London compared to 35% of those in London. Similarly, walking was slightly more common among workers in other parts of the UK than in London, with respective figures of 10% and 8%. In contrast, London commuters relied on buses more than their counterparts across the UK, making up around 12% and 8%, respectively. Meanwhile, cycling remained equally uncommon throughout the country, as only 5% of workers cycled to work. Lastly, trains and the underground were used by similar proportions of London workers, at around one-fifth, whereas these modes of transport were barely used in the rest of the UK, with both serving less than 5% of workers.
